articles.title: Consumer Fight Back - Black Friday - are you really saving money? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Black Friday promises huge savings, but are the deals really as good as they seem?
articles.body:
Radio Ulster , · 14 Nov 2026 , · 56 mins

Black Friday promises huge savings, but are the deals really as good as they seem? Before you click 'buy' Linzi Lima discusses the misleading discounts and marketing tactics that could leave shoppers paying more than they bargained for. Luxury serums, miracle ingredients and skincare routines costing hundreds of pounds. But when it comes to healthy skin, does a bigger price tag really mean better results? We separate the science from the hype... Why do some products just not last like they used to? Like trainers that fall apart after a few wears - many consumers feel quality is slipping. As trusted heritage brands change hands and manufacturing is outsourced, we investigate what's driving the decline and hear from the founder of the website 'Worse on Purpose' about the growing problem. Would you rather stream your music or own it? In an age of playlists and subscriptions, more people are returning to vinyl records, CDs and other physical formats. We'll explore what's behind the revival and why music fans are once again choosing something they can hold in their hands. Complaints about parcel deliveries are on the rise, and now Ofcom is warning companies to raise their game or face tighter regulation. We hear from James Stinson of Ofcom in Belfast. And if you've got a consumer issue, a story to share, or a question you'd like us to investigate, get in touch: cfb@bbc.co.uk

articles.title: What does Neet stand for and how many are there in the UK?
articles.summary: Ministers want to tackle the high number of young people not in education, employment or training.
articles.body:
There were 981,000 young people aged 16 to 24 not in employment, education or training between April and June, according to the latest data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS).

Figures published earlier in the year showed the number had previously topped one million, as an independent review warned of "a lost generation" of young people, unless urgent action is taken to support them.

A young person is considered Neet if they are n ot in e ducation, e mployment or t raining.

To be considered Neet, a person must be aged 16 to 24 and:

economically inactive - not actively looking for work and not waiting to start a job, or caring for family

not in formal education, such as school or university, or on a vocational course

not participating in any training schemes, such as apprenticeships or internships

Want your job application to stand out? Employers say they look for these six skills

Opportunities shrinking for too many young people, says major report on 'lost generation'

There were 981,000 Neets between April and June, the ONS says, an increase of about 3% on the same period in 2025.

The numbers are published every three months and vary throughout the year, but have been steadily increasing over time.

The latest figures account for 13% - over one in eight - of all young people in the UK.

There were more Neets classed as not looking or available for work than there were hunting for jobs.

The number of economically inactive young people was 588,000. This group includes 310,000 women and 278,000 men.

The ONS estimates that 393,000 16- to 24-year-olds were unemployed and looking for work. There were more unemployed young men than young women - 252,000 men compared with 141,000 women.

An estimated one in 10 young people who are Neet are graduates. However, those who have not achieved GCSE-level qualification are more likely to remain Neet for longer periods, according to the Youth Futures Foundation, an organisation which aims to ensure young people can find work.

It said those living in poverty, or with special educational needs, are also more likely to be Neet.

The ONS releases figures on the number of Neets in the UK every three months.

It produces its estimates from its Labour Force Survey. Fewer people have responded to the survey in recent years, which makes the results more volatile than in the past. The number of Neets tends to fluctuate throughout the year.

What needs to change to get more people working?

Five tips to help you get your first job

Why are there so many Neets and what is the impact?

A major independent review of the reasons so many young people are not in education, work or training was released by former Health Secretary Alan Milburn in May. He was asked to look into the issue by the government.

Milburn challenged the idea that young people were not trying, or were "work-shy, snowflakes, soft".

A survey carried out for his interim report suggested that 84% of Neet young people do want a job or training.

He said rejections for young jobseekers, after submitting dozens, sometimes hundreds of applications, had become the norm.

The report said there is not one factor causing the crisis, with a "perfect storm" of the jobs market, spending on education and the Covid pandemic being some of the reasons highlighted.

It said the number of entry-level jobs has fallen by about 1.6 million over the past 20 years. Vacancies in hospitality, for example, have halved in the last four years alone. Apprenticeships and graduate jobs have also been affected.

Health issues are also a factor. The proportion of people who say they are Neet because of a work-limiting health condition has increased by 70% over the past decade, according to the Health Foundation charity.

The proportion of Neets citing a mental health condition has more than doubled since 2012 to one in five, according to the most recent Labour Force Survey .

Milburn described the situation for young people with disabilities as "devastating". In 2024-2025, 29.6% of disabled young people were Neet, compared with 8.7% of their non-disabled peers, his report said.

The second part of Milburn's report, containing recommendations, will be unveiled later in 2026.

What is an apprenticeship and how much is the pay?

'I applied for 647 jobs after uni until I got one'

What is the government doing about Neets?

Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden welcomed Milburn's report and said the government was already taking action.

He said the government's job guarantee was supporting those "most in need", with the first young people who were supported by the scheme now in work.

"Our wider £2.5bn investment will help create almost a million opportunities to earn or learn," he said, adding that further reforms would follow the full Milburn review.

The government also announced a bursary of up to £4,500 for some families who would lose out on money if their children wanted to do an apprenticeship, because the child benefit they would lose out on would be worth more than the apprenticeship starter salary.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has also promoted a new work experience scheme by Sainsbury's, with 10,000 places being rolled out from October 2026.

However, shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately criticised the government's policies, claiming Labour had "destroyed job opportunities for young people" through increased taxes, such as employer National Insurance contributions .

Liberal Democrat Treasury spokesperson Daisy Cooper said her party "repeatedly warned that Labour's jobs tax would hammer job opportunities for young people and that their business rates hikes would kill off high street job opportunities".

Youth to get 'guaranteed' training in jobs overhaul

Inquiry to review rise in young people not working or studying

In Wales , the Young Person's Guarantee was introduced in 2021 to help 16- to 24-year-olds choose the right course, find an apprenticeship, search for jobs or start a business.

In Scotland , the Developing the Young Workforce (DYW) scheme was announced in the wake of the Covid pandemic to connect young people with appropriate opportunities such as apprenticeships, work experience or formal volunteering.

In Northern Ireland , there are a range of schemes aimed at helping Neets.

How do other countries help young people find work?

In his interim report, Milburn said the number of young people out of work, training or education in the UK is three times higher than in the Netherlands and twice as high as in Ireland.

A 2025 report from the Youth Futures Foundation said the Neet rate in the Netherlands has been steadily under 5% in the last decade.

It said the Netherlands has implemented significant reforms to support youth unemployment over the past two decades, including employment incentives like wage subsidies.

Interventions at national and regional levels include financial support, tailored career guidance, vocational training and structural reforms.

Career guidance in the Netherlands is mandatory in secondary school, and includes information on vocational education, the report said.

articles.title: PML-N set to form 'government' in PoK after two former 'premiers' lose strongholds in third phase
articles.summary: Two former so-called prime ministers of Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) lost their traditional strongholds in the third phase of elections, according to
articles.body: Two former so-called prime ministers of Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) lost their traditional strongholds in the third phase of elections, according to unofficial results released on Tuesday, while incumbent premier Faisal Mumtaz Rathore of the Pakistan People's Party (PPP) retained his seat.The latest results came after voting in four constituencies on Monday, with the election process again overshadowed by violence and allegations of rigging. Polling in the remaining seven constituencies was postponed over concerns about the law-and-order situation and is expected to be held on August 21, according to the region's election commission.The PPP won two of the four seats contested in the third phase, while the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and the Awami Dast-o-Bazu Party won one each. The latter is backed by both Jamaat-e-Islami and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI).Former prime minister and Muslim Conference president Sardar Attique Ahmed Khan, who was backed by the PML-N, lost the seat in Western Bagh's Dhirkot constituency to Awami Dast-o-Bazu Party candidate Sardar Sajid Iqbal, according to unofficial results. The seat had been held by the Muslim Conference/PML-N since 1985.In Central Bagh, PPP's Zia Qamar retained the seat, defeating PML-N candidate Mushtaq Minhas. Former premier Sardar Tanveer Ilyas, who joined the Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party, secured only a few thousand votes.The result in Eastern Bagh remained pending after authorities ordered a re-poll at 12 polling stations. PML-N candidate Sardar Mir Akbar was leading based on results from 174 of the constituency's 186 polling stations, followed by PPP candidate Sardar Qamaruz Zaman Khan.The election comes against the backdrop of a striking shift in the Pakistani government's treatment of the protest movement that has rocked PoK for months.Just days before the final phase of voting, Pakistan's defence minister Khawaja Asif had described the protesters as "enemies of Pakistan" and ruled out talks with them. But Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's adviser Rana Sanaullah subsequently said 99% of those associated with the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) were "patriotic brothers", promising that a PML-N government would engage with the group and seek to resolve its demands.The reversal in rhetoric came as the PML-N emerged as the dominant force in the election and prepared to form the next government in the region. The party has secured 25 of the 45 directly elected seats so far, while the PPP has won 12 and the Awami Dast-o-Bazu Party one.The first two phases, held on July 27 and August 2, were also marked by violent protests and allegations of widespread rigging, with the PML-N and PPP accusing each other of electoral malpractice. Supporters of the two parties clashed at several polling stations.The JAAC has been protesting across the region since early June, with demands including the abolition of 12 refugee seats that it says can be used to influence the formation of governments in PoK.The group has alleged that more than 40 people were killed during violence surrounding the first phase of voting and that around 400 protesters had been killed since the protests began. The Pakistani government has rejected the higher figure as exaggerated, while Sanaullah has acknowledged that deaths from the unrest were in the "double figures".India does not recognise Pakistan's control over the territory, maintaining that Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh are integral and inalienable parts of India and describing Pakistan's presence in areas under its control as "illegal and forcible occupation".Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: MUMBAI: National Congress Party leader and MLC Zeeshan Siddique filed a complaint soon after he arrived in Mumbai on Friday morning after a fresh threat he received while he was in London at 2.36 (which was 7.06 am IST).Bandra police registered a non-cognisable (NC) offence against an unknown person based on an audio threat he received on August 12.Siddique received the threat audio clip from a Portugal number.Siddique confirmed TOI that Bandra police registered an NC based on the complaint he submitted."The audio threat that lasted 1.29 minutes was received on my WhatsApp number by the same person who identified himself as Zeeshan Akhtar. My sister filed the first NC on August 6 while I was abroad. Now, the death threat audio clip was sent directly to me using Portugal number. In November 2025, we filed the writ and soon my security cover was reduced from eight cops to two. Also, there was 22 cops deployed at my residence which was reduced to zero," he said.The person who sent the audio threat dared Siddique to go and file a police complaint himself instead of sending his sister forward to file the complaint and threatened he will the one to kill him.TOI extracts the transcript of the threat audio which states, "Listen here, Zeeshan Siddique, this is Zeeshan Akhtar speaking. Listen to me carefully: I am going to kill you. Before I even touch your father... well, I had already assigned a team to the task two years ago, back when I was in police custody, got it?""Brother, everyone I’ve killed, I did so openly. Now, your end has come. Don't push your sister to the forefront; if you have the guts, go file the complaint yourself. I know everything; I’m aware of every detail. You might not die today or tomorrow, but within a year, you will definitely die. I have no problem with your money and I am not threatening you for money. The person claimed that he object to my illegal business and for which he will kill me. He threatened: 'You will die, and I am the one who will kill you'," the transcript stated further.The first threat compaint was filed by Siddique's sister Arshia on August 6. She was in the Bombay High Court (HC) for the hearing of a writ petition filed for initiating action against a builder whose role is suspected behind their father's murder."This is not coincidence. Both the threats are being made when the dates for the writ petition was nearing," he said.DCP (West Zone-2) Mohit Garg confirmed about the fresh NC registered on complaint from Siddique.A case of criminal intimidation involving severe threats, such as threatening death and grievous hurt was registered against unknown person.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: A Costa Rican mother saved for 9 years to buy land, then built her home with 7 tonnes of recycled plastic
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Cindy Mora Abarca spent 9 years saving money for a small plot of land in the Lámparas neighbourhood of Alajuelita, near San José, Costa Rica, hoping t.
articles.body: Cindy Mora Abarca spent 9 years saving money for a small plot of land in the Lámparas neighbourhood of Alajuelita, near San José, Costa Rica, hoping to eventually build a permanent home for herself and her 6-year-old son, Fabrizio. She eventually secured the land through a loan, but that left her without enough money to construct a house on it. Her situation changed when she connected with Habitat for Humanity Costa Rica, which paired her case with Procter & Gamble, the local organisation Urbarium and recycled materials group Ekojunto. Together, the partners built a home using interlocking blocks made primarily from recycled plastic waste, giving Mora and her son a permanent place to live. Construction began in April 2018, and the completed house was handed over to the family on May 26 this year. The project turned thousands of kilograms of discarded plastic into the walls of a real family home, while also demonstrating how recycled materials could be incorporated into conventional residential construction. The house became more than a solution to Mora’s immediate housing needs. It also demonstrated how waste that might otherwise end up in landfills or waterways could be redirected into useful building materials. The project offered a practical example of combining affordable housing with environmental goals, showing how recycling initiatives can have a direct social impact. The initiative also highlighted how partnerships between charities, businesses and local organisations can turn an environmental challenge into tangible support for families in need. This innovative approach to affordable housing offers a promising model for addressing both plastic pollution and housing shortages simultaneously, benefiting families and the environment together. Mora’s new home showed how environmental innovation can be paired with community support to create practical solutions that address two challenges at once.How recycled plastic was turned into the home's wallsAccording to reporting by La Nación, the house used approximately 7 tons of recycled plastic, with the material supplied through Procter & Gamble's corporate social responsibility programme. The plastic was processed into interlocking construction units known as Bloqueplas, a system developed to allow the pieces to fit together much like Lego blocks. Andrea Ramírez of Urbarium described the construction method as a practical way to transform plastic waste into building material rather than simply sending it for disposal. Recent retellings of the project commonly cite around 850 blocks, although the original Costa Rican reporting primarily emphasised the roughly 7 tons of recycled plastic used in the construction. The plastic blocks formed the home's walls, while conventional materials and methods were still used for the foundation, roof, plumbing, electrical wiring, doors and windows. Once the structure was completed and finished with plaster and paint, the house looked much like any other modest home in the surrounding neighbourhood rather than resembling an experimental recycling project.Why the claim that 800 volunteers built the house is misleadingOne detail that has repeatedly become distorted as the story has resurfaced online is the claim that 800 volunteers built the home. The original reporting describes more than 800 combined hours of volunteer labour, primarily contributed by Procter & Gamble employees, rather than 800 individual people working on the house. That distinction is important because the two figures describe completely different scales of participation. Habitat for Humanity Costa Rica was involved in selecting Mora's family based on socioeconomic need and ensuring that the property met the necessary requirements for construction, while Urbarium coordinated the local implementation of the recycled plastic block system. Volunteers then contributed their labour during the construction process, working alongside the organisations involved in the project. The home was therefore the result of a partnership between a housing organisation, a private company, local specialists and volunteers, rather than hundreds of people independently coming together to construct a house from plastic.What the plastic-block home was designed to demonstrateThe project was presented as an example of how plastic waste could be diverted into a useful, durable construction material while helping provide affordable housing. Urbarium publicly attributed several additional properties to its block system, including resistance to seismic forces, thermal and acoustic insulation and protection against weather. Those claims, however, should be treated as claims made by the organisation involved in the project, rather than independently verified characteristics of Mora's specific house; no independent testing specific to the home has been identified. The blocks were also designed to comply with Costa Rica's 2010 seismic construction code, according to project materials. For Mora, however, the environmental experiment was secondary to the practical outcome. After spending years saving for land and then struggling to afford construction, she finally had a permanent home where she could raise her son. The project became an early documented example in Costa Rica of recycled plastic being incorporated into a functioning residential building, showing that discarded material could become part of a home's physical structure rather than simply being treated as waste.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Nepal Speaker orders PM Balen to face House on Aug 26; attended just 5 of 39 sittings
articles.summary: South Asia News: Nepal Speaker Dol Prasad Aryal has ordered PM Balendra Shah to appear before the country's House of Representatives on Aug 26 and answer lawmakers dir.
articles.body: Nepal Speaker Dol Prasad Aryal has ordered PM Balendra Shah to appear before the country's House of Representatives on Aug 26 and answer lawmakers directly, issuing a rare parliamentary rebuke to a PM who attended just five of the first 39 sittings since taking office and faced months of opposition protests over his absence and controversial remarks on the India-Nepal border.Aryal issued the directive after repeated demands from opposition lawmakers for Shah to face Parliament. “I rule that the right honourable prime minister attend the meeting of the House of Representatives and answer questions from honourable members,” he said. The ruling ended a 77-day opposition protest over Shah's failure to clarify his border remarks. Under House rules, the first hour of one sitting in the first week of every month is reserved for lawmakers to directly question the PM.Opposition parties had been demanding Shah's presence since May, accusing him of avoiding parliamentary scrutiny. Lawmakers have also questioned his continued absence during a debate on communal unrest in Sunsari, where four people were killed, in the last week of July.Nepali Congress whip Nischal Rai had warned that opposition protests would continue unless Shah appeared before the House. “Has the PM escaped questions and tried to weaken democracy?” Rai asked, adding, “If the prime minister remains absent, the protest will continue.”Shah's May 31 appearance triggered a bigger confrontation. Responding to a question on Nepal's border dispute with India, Shah said, “After becoming PM, I came to know that not only has India encroached on Nepal’s land, but Nepal has also encroached on India’s land.” He added: “Both sides need to sit down and look into the matter.”Opposition parties demanded evidence, withdrawal of the statement and an apology, arguing that it weakened Nepal's position on Kalapani, Lipulekh and Limpiyadhura. Shram Sanskriti Party lawmaker Harka Rai rejected a subsequent clarification by foreign minister Shishir Khanal, saying the person who made the mistake “must come and rectify it”. Khanal had told the House that Shah was referring to cross-border occupation and encroachment in no-man's-land areas rather than a formal Nepalese territorial claim over Indian land.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Reform UK councillor resigns, then withdraws after sending letter to wrong council
articles.summary: UK News: A Reform UK councillor who said she had received “very little or no training” for her role has withdrawn her resignation after mistakenly sending her .
articles.body: A Reform UK councillor who said she had received “very little or no training” for her role has withdrawn her resignation after mistakenly sending her letter to the wrong council.Christine Duffy, elected in May to represent the Town ward on Newcastle-under-Lyme Borough Council, submitted her resignation letter to Kidsgrove Town Council on August 4, the BBC reported.She later said she no longer intended to quit and would continue serving the residents who elected her.Resignation sent to wrong councilIn the letter, seen by the BBC, Duffy said she had decided to step down because she had received “very little or no training” for the role.However, the letter was delivered to Kidsgrove Town Council rather than Newcastle-under-Lyme Borough Council, where she serves as a councillor.Under Electoral Commission rules, a councillor cannot withdraw a resignation once it has been received by the relevant authority. Duffy, however, said she changed her mind before the letter reached the borough council's proper officer.Newcastle-under-Lyme Borough Council chief executive Gordon Mole confirmed that the resignation had not taken effect.“If a councillor wishes to resign then they must follow a specific process as set out in the Local Government Act 1972,” Mole said, adding that the letter had been hand-delivered to an incorrect address.“By the time it was received by me, as the proper officer, I had been notified that the content of the letter had been withdrawn and the councillor concerned continues to serve as a borough councillor.”Duffy says she will continue as councillorIn a statement shared by Reform UK Newcastle-under-Lyme, Duffy said she was not resigning and remained committed to representing the Town ward.“I am not resigning as the borough councillor for the Town ward and I remain committed to representing the residents who elected me,” she said.Duffy also said she was “appalled” that her resignation letter had been made public.According to the BBC, she claimed political rivals had used the letter in an attempt to force a by-election.Questions over how letter was made publicDuffy had previously served on Kidsgrove Town Council but left the authority in October 2024.Mole said he was seeking an explanation over how the letter, which Duffy considered private, was shared publicly by a third party.Kidsgrove mayor Mike Stubbs called for the matter to be investigated, saying the public was entitled to expect “competent, timely and transparent administration” from their local authority.He said the handling of the episode had reached a point where “confidence in the process is being undermined.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Nathan Cofnas, who exposed Cambridge professor Jason Arday’s plagiarism, suspended by Ghent University
articles.summary: UK News: Nathan Cofnas has been suspended by Ghent University after exposing plagiarism allegations against late Cambridge professor Jason Arday. The university is investigating his public statements regarding the case.
articles.body: Nathan Cofnas, who publicly exposed plagiarism allegations involving late Cambridge professor Jason Arday, has been suspended by Ghent University, with Cofnas saying he expects to be fired.Cofnas announced his suspension on X, writing: “I was just suspended by Ghent University. They will almost certainly fire me.” He said the suspension was ordered by Ghent University rector Petra De Sutter, a former Green Party leader.The move comes after Cofnas published a detailed analysis of Arday's academic work in July, alleging that parts of the professor's 2015 PhD thesis closely matched earlier academic material. His post, published on Substack, examined passages that he said were similar or identical to work by other scholars, including a 2009 dissertation by Paula Zwozdiak-Myers.Arday had acknowledged citation errors but denied intentional academic misconduct. He attributed problems with his doctoral work to inadequate supervision and his autism.The allegations prompted wider scrutiny of Arday's academic record. Cambridge University later announced an investigation into his academic qualifications and honorary appointments, after which Arday resigned.Arday was subsequently found dead on August 14.Ghent University said it would take action Ghent University said on August 19 that it was taking Cofnas's recent public statements about the Arday case “very seriously”.The university said it had decided to take “appropriate action within its powers and the applicable framework”, but did not provide details about what Cofnas was accused of doing.It also said it did not want to prejudge the outcome of the matter and would respect the confidentiality of the personnel process.Cofnas joined Ghent University as a postdoctoral researcher in 2026. His appointment had already attracted criticism from some staff and students over his views on hereditarianism and differences between groups.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: At 68, Sheila Consaul owns one of America’s most unusual homes, a century-old lighthouse standing in Lake Erie. During a conversation with Tiny House Giant Journey, she opened up about how she went from building a career in Washington, DC, to buying the Fairport Harbor West Lighthouse in Ohio for $71,010 at auction in 2011 and spending more than $300,000 restoring it.What began as an unusual idea for a vacation home eventually became a 15-year restoration project, with Consaul investing more than $300,000 in the property and turning it into a largely off-grid residence while preserving its historic character.Why Sheila Consaul decided to buy a lighthouseBefore taking on the lighthouse, Consaul had already restored a historic home, which helped fuel her fascination with old buildings and restoration. While working in Washington, DC, she began looking for a summer home that was historic, unusual and located on the water.The idea of buying a lighthouse sounded fascinating to her after she learned that the federal government was auctioning off historic lighthouses.In 2009, the Fairport Harbor West Lighthouse became available at auction, and Consaul began bidding. It took two years before she finally secured the property, officially taking ownership in 2011. The lighthouse had been built in 1925 and was nearly 3,000 square feet, larger than many of the other lighthouses she had considered.Consaul's winning bid was $71,010. She later used a $200,000 home equity loan to cover the purchase and initial renovation costs, according to documents reviewed by CNBC Make It.An abandoned lighthouse in terrible conditionWhen Consaul first took possession, the lighthouse had been unoccupied since the late 1940s and had fallen into serious disrepair.“There were no utilities, no furniture, no creature comforts of any kind,” she recalled.The windows were broken and boarded up, plaster was falling from the walls and the property was described by Consaul as dreary and sad. The building had also been vandalized during the decades it sat empty. Ohio History Connection notes that the restoration involved repairing original windows, replacing those beyond repair, preserving flooring and carrying out extensive interior and exterior work.Consaul's first night at the lighthouse was far from luxurious.“My first night in the lighthouse was quite a challenge,” she said, recalling how she slept on a sleeping bag on the floor.She spent more than $300,000 restoring the propertyConsaul estimates that she has spent more than $300,000 renovating the lighthouse, well beyond her initial $200,000 renovation budget.The work included rewiring the building, restoring windows, repairing original floors, painting the interior and exterior and installing systems that would allow her to live there without conventional utilities.The restoration eventually transformed the lighthouse into a roughly 3,000-square-foot property with three bedrooms, three full bathrooms, five levels and four staircases.The project was not completed overnight. Consaul has described the restoration as a years-long process, with work often limited to the warmer months because she only lives at the lighthouse seasonally. A 2026 profile by Fairfax County says she spent 15 years restoring the lighthouse.She does not own the landThere is another unusual aspect to Consaul's ownership: she owns the lighthouse structure, but not the land on which it stands.The land belongs to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and Consaul paid $2,500 for a 25-year lease.She has said that as long as she owns the lighthouse, she intends to continue offering private tours. If she is still there when the lease expires, she plans to renew it.For Consaul, owning the building also means accepting responsibility for its place in the local community.“One thing that was very important to me when I bought this lighthouse was that I understood that this was part of this community of Fairport Harbor,” she said.What it is like to live off-gridToday, the lighthouse operates largely off-grid.Consaul collects rainwater from the roof and stores it in a cistern. The water then goes through pumping, treatment and chlorination systems before being used in the home.The property also has composting toilets.Electricity comes from sustainable sources including solar power, with a generator available when necessary. Ohio History Connection has also noted the installation of a solar/wind system as part of the property's sustainable power setup.Getting basic supplies is another challenge.The lighthouse has no dock, so Consaul accesses it through Headlands Beach State Park, walking through the dunes and along the breakwater.“People ask me all the time, how do I get supplies here? How do I get groceries? My answer is a backpack,” she said.She explained that the beach is several inches thick and difficult to navigate with a cart, making a backpack easier for carrying supplies in and out.Over the years, friends and volunteers have also helped transport furniture, equipment and renovation materials to the lighthouse.The lighthouse has a dangerous historyThe attraction of lighthouses, Consaul says, comes partly from their history.Lighthouse keepers were responsible for keeping the beacon burning, monitoring marine traffic and helping protect people navigating the waters. Lake Erie and the other Great Lakes can experience sudden and dangerous storms, making the work of lighthouse keepers particularly important.“The mystique comes from the dark of night. Comes from the fog and the wind and the weather,” Consaul said.The remote setting, harsh weather and isolation were all part of the lighthouse-keeper experience.A lighthouse built to survive Lake ErieThe Fairport Harbor West Lighthouse was constructed in Buffalo, New York, and transported by ship down Lake Erie to northeast Ohio.The structure was built with thick walls, steel plating, steel girders, brick and cast iron. Its beacon was first lit on June 9, 1925, meaning the lighthouse celebrated its 100th anniversary in 2025.The lighthouse was designed to withstand the harsh weather conditions around Lake Erie and was built to last.Three lighthouse keepers lived at the property after it opened in 1925. They worked around the clock to maintain the beacon, initially using kerosene before the lighthouse was electrified in the late 1940s.Once electricity was brought in, the keepers no longer needed to live at the lighthouse and could return to the Coast Guard station on land.What the lighthouse looked like when keepers lived thereThe building's current rooms have very different functions from those they had a century ago.The first floor, now a living room, kitchen and dining area, was essentially a working space when the keepers lived there. They used coal for heating and electricity, with coal brought by ship and lifted into the building through a chain winch.The second floor was where the keepers lived. Their families generally remained in Fairport Harbor rather than living at the lighthouse, and the keepers worked shifts before returning to shore.Consaul has also identified what she believes were the original kitchen and pantry spaces. In the former kitchen, evidence of a stove and cast-iron sink remains, while horizontal marks on the walls suggest where pantry shelves were once installed.Historic treasures discovered insideDuring the restoration, Consaul preserved many original features, including hardwood floors and hexagonal bathroom tiles.She also discovered artifacts connected to the lighthouse's past.One was a crate panel dated May 27, 1943, marked as coming from Frigidaire in Dayton, Ohio. Consaul believes it was associated with a refrigerator shipped to the lighthouse that year.Another discovery was an old ladder marked “USLHS”, referring to the U.S. Lighthouse Service. The service merged with the Coast Guard in 1939, helping date the ladder to before that transition.The original fog horn is also preserved inside the lighthouse.The lantern room and 100-year-old beaconHigher up in the lighthouse is the lantern room, where keepers once serviced the original beacon.Consaul believes a large opening in the room was used to bring in the original Fresnel lens, the large glass-prism lens technology used in historic lighthouse beacons.Today, the lighthouse has a modern LED beacon that remains an active aid to navigation.The beacon is powered by solar energy and comes on every evening at dusk before switching off at dawn. It follows a set pattern of two seconds on and three seconds off.The U.S. Coast Guard continues to maintain the equipment.A weather station and a 360-degree viewThe top of the lighthouse also houses a National Weather Service weather station, which records information including temperature, wind speed and wind direction.Above the lantern room is the widow's walk, where visitors can walk around the structure and take in a 360-degree view of northeast Ohio.Because the lighthouse sits in the middle of Lake Erie, Consaul is also exploring wind power.“You get a lot of wind,” she said, explaining that she has been looking for equipment strong enough to withstand the area's powerful winds while still generating useful electricity.She lives there only during the warmer monthsDespite turning the lighthouse into a comfortable home, Consaul does not live there year-round.Because the property has no conventional heating or air conditioning, she generally spends about four and a half months there.She opens the lighthouse around Memorial Day weekend and usually closes it around Columbus Day weekend.Before winter arrives, she shuts the property down and secures its exterior cast-iron shutters and interior storm windows.“Once October, November comes on, it gets cold and windy and pretty dangerous and icy and snowy and you don't want to be here,” she said.Why she wants to preserve the lighthouseConsaul's restoration has become about more than creating a unique summer home. She sees herself as a temporary steward of a historic landmark.“There are only so many lighthouses left. We are not building more lighthouses,” she said.The Fairport Harbor West Lighthouse remains part of the local community, and Consaul has opened it for annual open houses and private tours.She said one of the most rewarding parts of the project is watching people who have looked at the lighthouse from the shore for decades finally get the chance to see inside.“One of the things I love most about this house is the actual structure. I love living in that history,” she said.After years of restoration, Consaul says she can finally spend more time enjoying the property rather than constantly working on it.For her, the lighthouse is not simply something she bought at auction, it is a piece of history she hopes to pass on.“I’m just a steward of Fairport Harbor West. I hope it will be here another hundred years,” she said. For Consaul, that hope is what has made every year of restoration, hard work and isolation worthwhile.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Lindsay Clancy is obviously not guilty’: Candace Owens blames ‘Big Pharma’ for postpartum psychosis as trial nears end
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Candace Owens has publicly backed Lindsay Clancy, saying she is “obviously not guilty” in the deaths of her three children. Owens blamed the doctors w.
articles.body: Candace Owens has publicly backed Lindsay Clancy, saying she is “obviously not guilty” in the deaths of her three children. Owens blamed the doctors who treated Clancy and the psychiatric medicines she was prescribed before the January 2023 killings. Her comments have resurfaced while Clancy’s murder trial in Massachusetts is nearing its final stage. Clancy has admitted killing Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months, but has pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity. Her defense says severe postpartum psychosis and the effects of multiple medicines left her unable to understand her actions.Candace Owens says Lindsay Clancy was put into ‘intentional psychosis’A 46-second clip shared by KanekoaTheGreat shows Owens explaining her view of the case. She said she reached that conclusion when Clancy was first arrested and the case became public in 2023.Owens said: “I made my thoughts clear on this the moment that she um was arrested, the moment that it made the news. Lindsey Clancy is obviously not guilty. There are a fleet of doctors who should be imprisoned for what they put her on. I regularly speak out against Big Pharma.”She further added, “They get away with murder all the time and in this case they are getting away with the murder of really her three children but also completely destroyed her life. Lindsey Clancy in my opinion is not guilty. Uh she was put into a an intentional psychosis when she probably just needed to give her kids away for a weekend to get better but they constantly give you these drugs that do not make things better. And the cocktail of 10 pharmaceuticals that she was on is absolute madness. Absolute madness.”Owens therefore places much of the blame on Clancy’s medical treatment. Her comments are an opinion, not a finding by the court. The trial has not established that doctors intentionally caused psychosis in Clancy.Lindsay Clancy trial focuses on postpartum psychosis and medicationClancy’s defense does not dispute that she caused the deaths of her three children at the family’s Duxbury, Massachusetts, home on January 24, 2023. Instead, her lawyers argue that she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis and should not be held criminally responsible.Court evidence has shown that Clancy received 30 prescriptions for 13 psychiatric medicines from several providers before the killings. Her defense has argued that the treatment failed to identify her worsening condition and that the combination of medicines may have made her mental state worse. Prosecutors have challenged parts of that account and argued that Clancy acted deliberately.The case has now reached its final stretch. Testimony ended on Thursday, August 20, with closing arguments expected early next week, according to CBS News. The jury must ultimately decide whether Clancy is legally responsible for the deaths.The case has also brought renewed attention to postpartum psychosis, a rare but serious condition that can involve hallucinations, delusions and major changes in behaviour. In Clancy’s case, experts have disagreed over her mental state and whether it removed her criminal responsibility.Owens’ comments come as the court prepares to hear the final arguments in a trial where the central question is not whether Clancy caused her children’s deaths, but what was happening in her mind when they occurred.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: Eight people aboard a twin-engine Cessna charter plane were killed after it crashed Thursday near a remote radar site in western Alaska, the Alaskan Command confirmed.The aircraft was flying from Anchorage to Cape Newenham when it went down, according to the National Transportation Safety Board.The aircraft, operated by Security Aviation, was headed to Cape Newenham, about 40 miles south of Goodnews Bay, according to Clint Johnson, the NTSB’s Alaska chief.The aircraft was carrying two pilots and six passengers, Johnson said.Johnson said the plane crashed on land near Cape Newenham Airport, an Air Force airstrip that provides access to the Long Range Radar Station.The NTSB, Alaska State Troopers and the Rescue Coordination Center were responding to the crash site, he added.The Alaska Rescue Coordination Center said it launched a search-and-rescue operation after receiving a report of an “aircraft incident” near the Cape Newenham Long Range Radar Site.The centre said further information would be released as it became available but did not respond to questions.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Meet Angus Johnstone, the Australian teacher who kept a kite in the air for more than 26 hours to raise money for Myanmar
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Australian teacher and kite enthusiast Angus Johnstone has turned an unusual hobby into a Guinness World Records achievement and a fundraising campaig.
articles.body: Australian teacher and kite enthusiast Angus Johnstone has turned an unusual hobby into a Guinness World Records achievement and a fundraising campaign for Myanmar. In March 2026, Johnstone kept a kite airborne for 26 hours, 15 minutes and 15 seconds in Killarney, Victoria, earning the Guinness title for the longest kite flight by an individual. He began the attempt at 7:37 a.m. on March 14 and continued through an entire night before bringing the kite down the following morning. The challenge was also a personal mission for Johnstone, who previously lived and worked in Myanmar and met his wife there. He used the record attempt to raise money for grassroots health and education initiatives in Myanmar and among refugee communities along its borders.Angus Johnstone flew the kite through an entire nightJohnstone began the record attempt on March 14, 2026, in Killarney, Victoria, with a target of keeping his kite airborne for at least 24 hours. He ultimately exceeded that goal by more than two hours, completing the flight after 26 hours, 15 minutes and 15 seconds. During the attempt, he remained awake while sitting for long periods in a lawn chair and holding the kite line, carefully watching the kite as wind conditions changed. The challenge continued through daylight, sunset, darkness and a second sunrise. Stronger gusts eventually gave way to gentler nighttime winds, making it necessary for Johnstone to keep monitoring the kite's height, angle and movement. Guinness World Records officially recognised his achievement as the longest kite flight by an individual. The attempt was monitored by 10 official observers and two timekeepers, while friends and supporters worked in shifts to provide food, water and encouragement. Johnstone later told The Standard that he was "beyond tired" after completing the record, but said the excitement and support around him helped him continue.His love of kite flying began during the COVID pandemicJohnstone's record-breaking challenge grew from a hobby he developed during the COVID-19 pandemic, when restrictions limited many activities and kite flying offered him a way to spend time outdoors. He gradually became deeply interested in the hobby, joining online kite-flying communities, learning about different designs and collecting kites. His interest eventually developed into endurance flying and record attempts, but the 2026 challenge gave him an opportunity to connect his hobby with a cause that was personally important. Johnstone previously lived and worked in Myanmar, including time in Yangon and Lashio, and worked as a teacher there. He developed friendships during his years in the country and also met the woman who became his wife. His personal connection to Myanmar was the reason he decided to use the record attempt to raise money and awareness for communities affected by the country's ongoing humanitarian crisis.The record attempt raised thousands for MyanmarJohnstone's GoFundMe campaign, titled "Fly with Myanmar: World's Longest Kite Flight", has raised A$18,843 from 218 donations, exceeding its original A$18,000 target. The fundraiser says the money is intended to support grassroots health and education initiatives in Myanmar and among refugee communities along its borders. Johnstone's campaign comes as the country continues to face a severe humanitarian crisis involving armed conflict, displacement, disrupted services and economic hardship. The United Nations estimates that more than 16 million people will need humanitarian assistance in Myanmar in 2026, while the World Health Organization estimates that 9.3 million people will require health assistance. Johnstone has previously used unusual personal challenges to raise money for Myanmar, including a 2024 "Monobrows for Myanmar" campaign that raised more than A$4,000. The kite flight therefore became another unconventional way for him to combine his personal interests with fundraising for a country that remains closely connected to his life.Keeping a kite airborne for 26 hours was no easy taskAlthough kite flying can look effortless when conditions are favourable, maintaining a single kite in the air for more than a day requires careful attention to wind, height and angle. Johnstone had to remain awake throughout the attempt and respond as the weather changed from daytime conditions to a gentler nighttime breeze and back again. His support team helped monitor the attempt and keep him supplied with food and water, but Johnstone remained responsible for holding the kite line and keeping the kite airborne. Photographs from the challenge show supporters feeding him grapes while he continued flying, as well as Johnstone sitting under the night sky with the kite still visible above him. The attempt ended on March 15 after 26 hours, 15 minutes and 15 seconds, when Johnstone finally brought the kite back to the ground as supporters gathered to celebrate. The achievement is specifically the longest kite flight by an individual, rather than the longest kite flight overall, as Guinness World Records has separate categories for team attempts.A world record with a personal purposeFor Johnstone, the Guinness title was ultimately a way to draw attention to Myanmar while doing something he genuinely enjoys. The record gave his fundraising campaign an unusual hook, turning more than 26 hours of endurance flying into an opportunity to collect donations and highlight the needs of communities in a country where he once lived and taught. His achievement also shows how a hobby developed during the pandemic can evolve into an extraordinary endurance challenge with a humanitarian purpose. After more than a day of holding the kite line, staying awake and watching the wind, Johnstone finally brought the colourful kite back to the ground, securing a Guinness World Records title while raising thousands of Australian dollars for a cause with a deeply personal connection to him.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Jason Arday's death: Why a Ghent University academic is under probe after plagiarism accusation
articles.summary: US News: Postdoctoral researcher Nathan Cofnas, who made plagiarism allegations against ex-Cambridge professor Jason Arday before his death, has been suspended.
articles.body: Postdoctoral researcher Nathan Cofnas, who made plagiarism allegations against ex-Cambridge professor Jason Arday before his death, has been suspended by Ghent University.Arday had resigned from his position at the University of Cambridge this month following coverage of Cofnas’s plagiarism allegations. The claims were not established through any formal investigation, but prompted questions about Arday’s academic achievements.He was found dead at his residence in Battersea, south London, on August 14.Cambridge’s handling of the affair, along with its coverage by the media, came under intense scrutiny after Arday’s death. Cambridge chancellor Chris Smith described the episode as a “racist feeding frenzy”.Cofnas, described as an “American anti-woke” blogger, has been a postdoctoral researcher in Ghent University’s department of philosophy and moral sciences, according to his website.On Thursday, Cofnas wrote on X that he was being investigated by his university for discriminating against Arday. In a separate post, he said he had been suspended and expected to be dismissed.Ghent University confirmed the suspension after saying it had been “shocked” by Arday’s death and that the circumstances should prompt reflection. The university also said it opposed discrimination, hatred and racism.In a joint statement, rector Petra De Sutter and vice-rector Herwig Reynaert said the university valued academic freedom and open academic debate, including controversial views, but stressed that such freedom was not unlimited and came with responsibility.They said academic freedom could be restricted to protect the rights of others and that the university was taking Cofnas’s recent public statements “very seriously”.The university later said it had formally notified the staff member that a preliminary disciplinary investigation had begun. It is assessing whether there are sufficient grounds to refer the case to the competent disciplinary body.Cofnas has been suspended as a precaution while the preliminary investigation is under way.In 2024, Cofnas was also dismissed from his role at Emmanuel College, Cambridge. In blog posts, he had written that in a meritocracy, “Blacks would disappear from almost all high-profile positions outside of sports and entertainment.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.standfirst: Atendimento será realizado na segunda (16) e terça-feira (17), das 10h às 17h, no Auditório Municipal Alcides Rossi. Iniciativa também contempla mutuários com prestações em dia.
articles.summary: A campanha de renegociação CDHU em Itapetininga ocorre nos dias 16 e 17 de dezembro, com análise individual para reduzir o saldo devedor e ajustar as parcelas mensais.
articles.body:
A CDHU Móvel disponibiliza diversos serviços gratuitos aos mutuários — Foto: Agência SP/Reprodução

Moradores de Itapetininga (SP) com financiamento habitacional pela Companhia de Desenvolvimento Habitacional e Urbano (CDHU) poderão regularizar parcelas atrasadas e renegociar as condições do contrato durante a campanha Casa em Dia, que será realizada na segunda-feira (16) e terça-feira (17).

O atendimento será das 10h às 17h, no Auditório Municipal Alcides Rossi, anexo ao Paço Municipal, no Jardim Marabá.

A iniciativa oferece alternativas de negociação sem a necessidade de pagamento de entrada. A campanha é voltada tanto para mutuários com prestações em atraso quanto para aqueles que estão com os pagamentos em dia, mas desejam conhecer outras possibilidades para o financiamento.

Durante o atendimento, a CDHU fará uma análise individual de cada contrato. Entre as possibilidades estão a regularização de parcelas atrasadas, a redução do saldo devedor, a adequação das prestações à renda familiar e a fixação dos valores das parcelas até o fim do financiamento.

As condições disponíveis dependem da situação de cada contrato e da análise dos documentos apresentados. A simulação permite que o mutuário conheça as alternativas antes de decidir pela renegociação.

Para solicitar uma simulação, os interessados devem apresentar:

RG e CPF ou Carteira Nacional de Habilitação (CNH);

Os três últimos holerites ou comprovantes de renda;

Cadastro Nacional de Informações Sociais (CNIS);

Declaração de benefício do INSS, quando aplicável.

Outros documentos poderão ser solicitados conforme a composição familiar e a situação do financiamento.

Além do atendimento presencial durante a campanha, os mutuários podem procurar as unidades regionais da CDHU ou entrar em contato com a Central Alô CDHU, pelo telefone 0800 000 2348.

Outras informações sobre os canais de atendimento estão disponíveis no site da CDHU

articles.title: Falha em foguete destrói 40 satélites da Amazon que seriam usados em serviço rival da Starlink | G1
articles.standfirst: Falha no foguete Vulcan, cerca de 10 minutos após a decolagem na Flórida, destruiu a carga e representa um revés para os planos da empresa de lançar seu serviço de internet via satélite ainda em 2026.
articles.summary: Falha no foguete Vulcan, cerca de 10 minutos após a decolagem na Flórida, destruiu a carga e representa um revés para os planos da empresa de lançar seu serviço de internet via satélite ainda em 2026.
articles.body:
Uma carenagem de carga útil da United Launch Alliance (ULA), que transporta uma espaçonave de segurança nacional a ser acoplada a um foguete Vulcan para a missão USSF-87, é transportada por uma via no Centro Espacial Kennedy, em Cabo Canaveral, Flórida (EUA). — Foto: Brendan McDermid/Reuters

Amazon planejava usar esses satélites para iniciar seu serviço de internet Amazon Leo , concorrente da Starlink, ainda em 2026. A Amazon perdeu 40 satélites de seu serviço de internet Amazon Leo no domingo (15) devido a uma falha no foguete de lançamento.

O foguete Vulcan, da United Launch Alliance (ULA), uma joint venture da Boeing e da Lockheed Martin, falhou pouco depois da decolagem, destruindo sua carga de 40 satélites da rede de internet Amazon Leo.

O foguete apresentou problemas cerca de 10 minutos após a decolagem da Estação de Cabo Canaveral, na Flórida, e a causa ainda é desconhecida .

Desde 2025 foram colocados em órbita 398 satélites do Amazon Leo em 14 lançamentos , o equivalente a cerca de 12% do plano total da empresa. A Amazon havia anunciado planos de usar esses satélites para iniciar seu serviço comercial de internet ainda em 2026.

O incidente representou um grande revés para o novo foguete principal da ULA, fundada há duas décadas, justamente quando a empresa buscava iniciar um ritmo regular de lançamentos para a internet via satélite da Amazon.

Essa foi a primeira falha de missão da empresa de lançamentos.

A Amazon adquiriu 38 lançamentos da ULA e, no longo prazo, o Vulcan deverá colocar em órbita quase metade da primeira geração de satélites do Amazon Leo, composta por 3.232 unidades.

O lançamento fracassado de domingo levaria ao espaço o maior lote de satélites já enviado pela Amazon, que não realizava lançamentos desde julho. Para o Vulcan, foi o quinto voo desde sua estreia, em 2024, e o primeiro em nove meses.

O contratempo ocorreu um dia depois de a SpaceX, de Elon Musk, colocar em órbita 26 satélites da sua rede de internet, a Starlink, durante um voo de teste do foguete Starship, realizando pela primeira vez a "captura" de uma nave espacial em voo para demonstrar a viabilidade de foguetes reutilizáveis.

O foguete New Glenn, da Blue Origin, no qual a Amazon também aposta para seus lançamentos, está fora de operação desde uma explosão ocorrida durante um teste em maio.

Sucessivas falhas de foguetes têm atrasado persistentemente a tentativa da Amazon de competir com a vasta rede de internet Starlink, que conta com mais de 11 mil satélites e milhões de clientes em todo o mundo.

articles.title: Buraco em Sumaré: rompimento de tubulação causou queda de pedestres | G1
articles.standfirst: Caixa de inspeção de galeria de águas pluviais se rompeu na Avenida da Amizade, em Sumaré. Córrego canalizado passa por baixo da calçada onde ocorreu o acidente.
articles.summary: O buraco em Sumaré que engoliu uma mulher com bebê e um homem foi causado pelo rompimento de uma galeria pluvial; populares ajudaram no resgate das vítimas com cordas.
articles.body:
O buraco que se abriu na calçada e "engoliu" um homem e uma mulher que carregava uma criança no colo , na manhã desta segunda-feira (16), em Sumaré (SP), foi provocado pelo rompimento de uma caixa de inspeção da galeria de águas pluviais , segundo a prefeitura. A estrutura fica na Avenida da Amizade , no bairro Parque da Amizade.

A caixa faz parte de um sistema subterrâneo que recebe a água da chuva e de um córrego canalizado que passa pela região . Segundo o secretário municipal de Obras, Fernando Luis Pereira, o curso d'água passa por baixo de uma praça esportiva próxima ao local, segue pelo canto da calçada onde ocorreu o acidente, atravessa a rua e deságua no Ribeirão Quilombo.

"Identificamos que a caixa de inspeção da galeria de águas pluviais foi rompida e nós estamos com a equipe aqui, fizemos as análises juntamente com a equipe de engenharia do departamento de Obras e já vamos começar a manutenção", afirmou o secretário.

De acordo com Fernando, o volume de chuvas das últimas horas pode ter contribuído para o rompimento da estrutura.

Pode ocasionar algum tipo de problema em relação a isso [chuva], mas nós já estamos tomando todas as providências necessárias e vamos iniciar a manutenção já, disse.

Calçada cede e ‘engole’ mulher com criança no colo e homem em Sumaré — Foto: Circuito de segurança

Após identificar o rompimento, equipes municipais foram ao local para avaliar as condições da estrutura subterrânea e a extensão dos danos . Engenheiros da Secretaria de Obras também verificam se a erosão atingiu a estrutura da padaria que fica em frente ao ponto onde a calçada cedeu.

A vistoria contou com a participação da Defesa Civil e do Departamento de Obras. Segundo a prefeitura, equipes da Administração Regional e representantes da BRK Ambiental também acompanham os trabalhos para avaliar as possíveis causas do problema e definir os reparos necessários.

Acidente foi registrado por câmera de segurança

Uma câmera de segurança de uma padaria registrou o momento em que a mulher, que carregava uma criança no colo, e um homem caíram na cratera.

Nas imagens, a mulher apareceu saindo do estabelecimento e parando por alguns instantes para falar com alguém que estava dentro da padaria. Em seguida, parte da calçada cedeu e abriu o buraco, fazendo com que ela e a criança caíssem. Um homem que passava pelo local também caiu.

Segundo a dona da padaria, Conceição Aparecida Pereira, comerciantes da região se mobilizaram para retirar as vítimas antes da chegada das equipes de socorro . Eles utilizaram uma corda e uma escada para ajudar no resgate.

"A moça estava com a perna bem machucada, a menininha estava bem. O moço estava com a cabeça bem machucada", relatou.

A comerciante contou que a criança foi retirada primeiro. Em seguida, os populares ajudaram a mulher e o homem a sair do buraco.

O Corpo de Bombeiros informou que, quando a equipe chegou, as vítimas já haviam sido retiradas. A mulher apresentava escoriações nas pernas, principalmente na região dos joelhos e dos pés. A criança aparentemente não tinha ferimentos, mas também foi encaminhada ao hospital para passar por exames.

As três vítimas foram levadas à UPA Macarenko: a mulher, pelo Samu (Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência); a criança, pelo pai; e o homem, por meios próprios.

Mulher com criança no colo e homem caem após abertura de buraco em Sumaré — Foto: Câmeras de segurança

O afundamento provocou alterações no trânsito da Avenida da Amizade. O trecho próximo à cratera foi isolado, e os motoristas precisaram utilizar um desvio durante os trabalhos das equipes.

A Secretaria Municipal de Mobilidade Urbana e Rural (SMMUR) acompanhou a circulação de veículos e orientou os motoristas durante a interdição.

articles.title: França vai pedir sanções contra o Irã após ataque a supermercados | G1
articles.standfirst: Governo apresentará evidências a ministros da União Europeia e pedirá novas sanções contra Teerã. Paris quer definir lista de alvos em até um mês.
articles.summary: França apresentará à União Europeia evidências de participação iraniana em ataque cibernético contra sistemas de refrigeração de supermercados e pedirá novas sanções.
articles.body:
Imagem do corredor de congelados fechado em um supermercado próximo a Nantes, após um ataque cibernético que teve como alvo os sistemas de refrigeração de redes de supermercados francesas, causando perdas de alimentos e incêndios em várias lojas, na França, em 12 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Stephane Mahe

A França deve apresentar nesta segunda-feira (16) provas de que a Guarda Revolucionária Iraniana está por trás do ataque aos sistemas de refrigeração de supermercados franceses , segundo o chanceler francês, Jean-Noël Barrot. O país também pedirá a aplicação de novas sanções contra Teerã via União Europeia, ele disse.

O ministro das relações exteriores francês afirmou que pretende obter, em até um mês, uma lista de novas pessoas e entidades do Irã que poderão ser alvo das sanções. A declaração foi dada ao chegar a uma reunião mensal de ministros das Relações Exteriores do bloco europeu, em Bruxelas, na Bélgica.

Em outubro, hackers elevaram a temperatura de muitos refrigeradores de supermercados franceses para 50 graus Celsius durante a noite , causando incêndios e perdas de alimentos em centenas de lojas em todo o país.

A Procuradoria de Paris afirmou que o ataque de "grande escala" afetou os sistemas de refrigeração conectados em diversas grandes redes de supermercados na França.

💻 Os sistemas de refrigeração dos supermercados geralmente são operados por painéis de controle que gerenciam todas as geladeiras e freezers de uma loja e podem ser acessados pela internet, permitindo que empresas de manutenção façam ajustes remotamente, de qualquer lugar.

A França apresentou as acusações na semana passada e convocou o embaixador iraniano no país para prestar esclarecimentos. Na segunda-feira passada, o Ministério Público Francês emitiu mandados de prisão internacionais contra o líder da Shahid Kaveh, uma unidade de operações cibernéticas ofensivas ligada à Guarda Revolucionária iraniana, e seus dois principais subordinados.

Os ataques acontecem em meio a uma onda de invasões e ataques cibernéticos ao redor do mundo. No último sábado (14), o serviço de entregas francês La Poste confirmou que sofreu um vazamento de dados que atingiu cerca de 22 milhões de pessoas , equivalente a um terço da população francesa.

articles.title: Prefeito associa crise no Rio Poti a esgoto; empresa nega falhas | G1
articles.standfirst: Arsete solicitou análise da água do rio, com resultado previsto para quarta-feira (18); concessionária afirma que monitoramento próprio não aponta alterações na qualidade hídrica.
articles.summary: Silvio Mendes aponta poluição no Rio Poti como causa da morte de peixes e aguapés, mas concessionária garante que tratamento de esgoto segue normas ambientais.
articles.body:
O prefeito de Teresina , Silvio Mendes (União Brasil), relacionou a proliferação de aguapés e a mortandade de peixes registradas nos últimos dias à poluição do Rio Poti. Nesta segunda-feira (16), o gestor questionou a qualidade do tratamento do esgoto lançado no rio. Procurada pelo g1 , a Águas de Teresina afirmou que todo o esgoto coletado passa por tratamento e que cumpre as normas ambientais.

Em entrevista à TV Clube , Silvio Mendes afirmou que a presença de aguapés é um indicativo da poluição do Rio Poti. Segundo o prefeito, a degradação da água pode estar relacionada à mortandade de peixes e de outros organismos que vivem no rio. O gestor também defendeu uma atuação conjunta da Prefeitura de Teresina, do Governo do Estado e do Governo Federal para enfrentar o problema.

Ao g1 , a Águas de Teresina afirmou que a estação de tratamento de esgoto (ETE) Leste possui licenças e outorga para lançamento de efluentes, além de realizar monitoramento diário e análises que, segundo a concessionária, comprovam que o despejo não altera a qualidade da água do Rio Poti.

A empresa também destacou investimentos superiores a R$ 1,5 bilhão em Teresina e reforçou a importância de os moradores conectarem seus imóveis à rede de esgoto para evitar o descarte irregular ( leia a íntegra da nota ao fim da reportagem ) .

"Soube hoje que esse tratamento desse esgoto não está sendo de forma adequada. Mesmo quando adequada, ele diminui o oxigênio da água, aumenta os elementos, principalmente o fósforo e o nitrogênio. A presença do aguapé é a certeza que a gente tem que a água é poluída, de má qualidade. Como consequência, a mortandade dos peixes, além dos outros seres vivos que tem lá", iniciou o prefeito.

Silvio Mendes afirmou ainda que questões sobre o Rio Poti são de responsabilidade da Agência Nacional de Águas e Saneamento Básico (ANA). Segundo ele, o órgão autorizou a Águas de Teresina a lançar efluentes no rio.

"Se comete um crime ambiental, no caso contra o Rio Poti, há muitos anos, e a natureza cobra o preço. A Agência Nacional de Águas, que um órgão do Governo Federal, é quem faz a gestão do rio e ela autorizou a Águas de Teresina a despejar no Rio Poti o esgoto que ela coleta", disse.

"O problema é: é um rio federal, por conta da Agência Nacional de Águas, e a Águas de Teresina continua colocando esgoto, tratado ou não, dentro do rio.", completou o gestor.

Para o prefeito, a união efetiva entre a prefeitura, o Governo do Estado e o Governo Federal pode ajudar a conter os problemas enfrentados pelo Rio Poti.

"O Estado e o Governo Federal, naturalmente precisa ter a união desses esforços para ver se a gente estanca essa repetição de agressão ao meio ambiente, no caso do Rio Poti", disse Silvio.

Um acordo judicial firmado em 2013 prevê o acompanhamento de um cronograma de ações voltadas à limpeza e ao saneamento dos rios Poti e Parnaíba.

Silvio Mendes informou ainda que a Agência Municipal de Regulação de Serviços Públicos de Teresina (Arsete) solicitou uma análise da qualidade da água do Rio Poti. Segundo o prefeito, o resultado deve ser divulgado na quarta-feira (18).

Peixes mortos em trecho do Rio Poti — Foto: Antônio Fernandes - TV Clube

A Águas de Teresina esclarece que todo o esgoto coletado pela empresa é tratado antes de ser devolvido ao meio ambiente, seguindo as exigências e os parâmetros estabelecidos pela legislação ambiental, especialmente pelas normas do Conselho Nacional do Meio Ambiente (CONAMA) e da Agência Nacional de Águas e Saneamento Básico (ANA).

A Estação de Tratamento de Esgoto (ETE) Leste possui todas as autorizações ambientais necessárias, incluindo outorga para o lançamento de efluente tratado. A unidade trata diariamente milhões de litros de esgoto, impedindo que esse volume seja lançado sem tratamento no Rio Poti. Todo o processo é acompanhado por monitoramento diário e análises laboratoriais que comprovam a eficiência do tratamento e a conformidade do efluente com os padrões ambientais exigidos.

A empresa também monitora a qualidade da água do Rio Poti antes e depois do ponto de lançamento do efluente tratado da ETE Leste. Os resultados das análises indicam que esse lançamento não altera a qualidade da água do rio.

Teresina possui o maior investimento per capita em saneamento entre as capitais do Nordeste, segundo dados do Instituto Trata Brasil. Desde o início da operação, a empresa já investiu mais de R$ 1,5 bilhão na cidade, e a rede de esgoto está disponível para cerca de 60% da população.

Nos locais onde a rede de esgoto já está disponível, a ligação dos imóveis ao sistema é fundamental para ampliar os benefícios do saneamento e reduzir o descarte irregular de esgoto em sarjetas, canais e outros pontos que podem contribuir para a poluição dos corpos hídricos do município.
